source: Every agent defers to some agent. Therefore there is an agent to whom every agent defers.

claims.text: Every agent defers to some agent.

translations.formula: (forall x (implies (Agent x) (exists y (and (Agent y) (Defers x y)))))
translations.reason: Translates 'Every agent defers to some agent' using universal and existential quantifiers with Agent and Defers predicates.

translations.formula: (exists y (and (Agent y) (forall x (implies (Agent x) (Defers x y)))))
translations.reason: Translates 'There is an agent to whom every agent defers' using existential and universal quantifiers with Agent and Defers predicates.

interpretation_notes: The domain includes all individuals, with Agent(x) restricting quantification to agents. The argument's validity depends on logical properties of quantifiers, not on the content of 'defers' or 'agent' predicates.

The translation preserves the original quantifier structure: premise c1 uses ∀∃ and conclusion c2 uses ∃∀, which is a classic case of invalid inference in classical logic (converse of the converse of a universal quantifier).
